signals.title: Untouched shadcn theme
signals.why: The stock radius and neutral ramp ship on thousands of sites, so the page inherits their face.
signals.fix: Pick your own radius and tint the neutrals toward a hue (even chroma 0.005 reads warmer or cooler than stock).

signals.title: This year's ‘tasteful’ display serif
signals.why: Instrument Serif, Fraunces and Playfair Display were the anti-slop fix for headings. Now every generator told to look editorial lands on them.
signals.fix: Pick a display serif from outside the current shortlist, or let the body face carry the headings.

signals.title: One accented word in the headline
signals.why: A single word in another colour, italic or gradient is how generated heroes say ‘this part matters’.
signals.fix: Set the headline in one voice. If a word matters, choose a word that carries it.

signals.title: Multicolour gradient text
signals.why: Clipped rainbow headlines are the generator's way of saying ‘important’. Readers have learnt to skim past them.
signals.fix: Set the text in one solid colour. A tonal ramp of one hue is fine; a hue jump is the tell.

signals.title: Pill above the headline
signals.why: A rounded badge over the H1 is in nearly every generated hero, whether or not there is news.
signals.fix: Ship it only for real, dated news that links somewhere, or move news to a changelog link in the header.

signals.title: Tracked all-caps labels everywhere
signals.why: Small spaced capitals over every section (FEATURES, PRICING, HOW IT WORKS) are the default way generators fake editorial structure.
signals.fix: Let the section heading do the work. Keep small caps for real metadata like dates or table headers.

hit.evidence: FEATURES, PRICING, TESTIMONIALS, FAQ set in caps at 0.12em

signals.title: Indigo-to-pink, the house colour
signals.why: Tailwind's indigo-500 became the colour of generated landing pages. It signals ‘AI product’ before anyone reads a word.
signals.fix: Use your brand hue. If you want a gradient, keep it within one hue family (under 40°).

signals.title: Gradients as decoration
signals.why: Coloured washes behind sections, cards and buttons fill space the content should fill.
signals.fix: Keep one gradient where it means something, or none. Flat surfaces read as more confident.

signals.title: Dark by default, untinted
signals.why: Near-black from the Tailwind ramp is the stock ‘premium’ look, not a decision, especially when it ignores the visitor's light preference.
signals.fix: Respect prefers-color-scheme, and tint the dark ground toward your brand hue.

signals.title: Cream and terracotta
signals.why: Warm cream with a terracotta accent is the newer generated look, borrowed from Anthropic's own palette.
signals.fix: If warm paper suits you, pair it with an accent from your own brand, not #D97757.

signals.title: Three rounded cards in a row
signals.why: Feature, feature, feature in identical rounded boxes is the generator's default rhythm for any content.
signals.fix: Let the content decide the layout: a list, a table, one large example, or uneven columns.

hit.evidence: 3 cards in one row, 16px radius, the same soft shadow (section.features > div)

signals.title: Icons in tinted tiles
signals.why: An icon on a pale tinted square above every feature is the single most recognisable generated pattern.
signals.fix: Use the icon inline with the title at text size, show the real product, or drop the icons.

signals.title: A row of big round numbers
signals.why: ‘10K+ users · 99.9% uptime · 4.9★’ is the default proof section, real numbers or not.
signals.fix: Show one number that matters with its source, or a real customer and what changed for them.

signals.title: 01 · 02 · 03 markers
signals.why: Zero-padded numbers on sections that aren't a sequence are editorial costume.
signals.fix: Number things only when order matters to the reader.

signals.title: Everything centred
signals.why: Centring every block removes the edge the eye reads from and makes every section look the same.
signals.fix: Centre the hero if you want, then align sections to a start edge with a clear column.

signals.title: Coloured stripe down the side of cards
signals.why: A thick coloured left border on cards and callouts is one of the most recognisable generated details.
signals.fix: Use a heading, an icon at text size or a background tint to mark the card, not a side stripe.

signals.title: Frosted glass on everything
signals.why: One frosted header is fine. Frosted cards, badges and buttons turn into a texture with no depth logic.
signals.fix: Keep backdrop blur for the one layer that actually floats over content, usually the sticky header.

signals.title: Coloured glows
signals.why: A soft coloured halo under buttons and cards is the default ‘cool’ of generated UI. Real light doesn't come from a button.
signals.fix: Use a neutral shadow that explains elevation, or none.

signals.title: Blurred orbs and halos
signals.why: Big blurred colour blobs behind the hero are filler that says ‘tech’ without showing anything.
signals.fix: Show the product, a real image, or let the type stand on a plain ground.

signals.title: Dot or grid wallpaper
signals.why: A tiled dot or line grid behind the hero is the stock way to make empty space look technical.
signals.fix: Keep grid lines for surfaces that are really a canvas, a map or a blueprint.

signals.title: Emoji standing in for icons
signals.why: 🚀 and ✅ at the start of nav links, headings and bullets come straight from chat output pasted into a page.
signals.fix: Use plain bullets, numbers or one line-icon set drawn at text size. Emoji belong in sentences, not in structure.

signals.title: The sparkles icon
signals.why: ✨ has become the universal ‘AI inside’ badge. It promises magic instead of saying what happens.
signals.fix: Replace it with an icon or word for what the feature actually does.

signals.title: A Lucide icon as the logo
signals.why: Generators fill the logo slot with whatever icon the library ships. A brand mark from a free icon set says the brand is a placeholder.
signals.fix: Draw a wordmark, even a plain one in a face you chose.

signals.title: Template marketing phrases
signals.why: Phrases that fit any product tell the reader nothing about this one.
signals.fix: Say what it does, for whom, in plain words, and name one specific thing it does better.

signals.title: Words a model reaches for
signals.why: Delve, tapestry, pivotal, testament to, serves as: each is fine once, but together they are the vocabulary of unedited model output.
signals.fix: Use the plain word: ‘is’ for ‘serves as’, ‘use’ for ‘leverage’, and cut praise the reader can't check.

signals.title: ‘Label: text’ in every bullet
signals.why: A bold label and a colon at the start of each list item is how chat answers structure everything, and it usually restates the line it opens.
signals.fix: Write the item as a sentence, or let a bold lead-in end in a full stop and add something new after it.

signals.title: Boilerplate social proof
signals.why: ‘Trusted by 10,000+ teams’ and ‘No credit card required’ are filled in by default, so readers discount them.
signals.fix: Name a real customer, link a real review, or leave it out until you have one.

signals.title: Em dashes in every sentence
signals.why: One em dash is good punctuation. One every few lines is the rhythm of generated prose.
signals.fix: Use full stops, commas and colons; keep the dash for real interruptions.

signals.title: ‘It's not X, it's Y’ and ‘not just X, but Y’
signals.why: The rebuttal cadence, repeated, is the most quoted tell of generated copy.
signals.fix: Say what it is. Skip the strawman.

signals.title: Leftovers from a template or a chat
signals.why: Lorem ipsum, ‘Feature 1’, raw **Markdown**, chatbot citation markers or ‘I hope this helps’ mean nobody read the page before it shipped.
signals.fix: Replace every placeholder with real content, delete the chat leftovers, or remove the section.

signals.title: Every section fades in on scroll
signals.why: The same fade-and-slide-up on every block is the default motion of generated pages, and it hides content from anyone who doesn't scroll slowly.
signals.fix: Show content at rest. Animate one thing that explains something, and respect reduced motion.

signals.title: Bouncy easing
signals.why: Overshooting curves make interfaces feel like toys. Generators add them to look ‘delightful’.
signals.fix: Use an ease-out with no overshoot for UI; save springs for things that are physically thrown.

signals.title: The starter's tab title, favicon or share tags
signals.why: The tab title, favicon and share card are the first things anyone sees of a page, and these are still the values the scaffolder or site builder wrote.
signals.fix: Give the page its own title, description, favicon and share tags.

signals.title: Lovable's starter tokens
signals.why: The generator's own prompt names these variables. Keeping them keeps its look.
signals.fix: Rename and redefine the tokens around your own palette and elevation.

signals.title: Copy-paste effect components
signals.why: Border beams, shimmer buttons, meteors and number tickers come from the same few registries every generator pulls from.
signals.fix: Keep one effect if it explains something; drop the rest.

signals.title: Placeholder and stock photo hosts
signals.why: Hotlinked Unsplash, picsum and pravatar images are what generators drop in when there is no real product to show.
signals.fix: Show the actual product, team or work. One real screenshot beats ten stock photos.
